title: Like water
hook: the highest good is like water: it benefits all and seeks the low places (Tao Te Ching 8)

segments.voice: Yesterday, chapter seven, and your line was last, and first. Did you get to wave someone ahead? Heaven and earth, the valley, the one who goes last: chapter eight gathers them into one picture. Day one thousand seventy.

A glass tips over at dinner. In a second the water is everywhere it can reach. It runs along the grain of the table, slips under the edge of a plate, finds the one low spot by the salt shaker, and drips off the corner onto the floor. Nobody told it where to go. It didn't argue with the plate. It went around. Water seems to know exactly where the lowest place is, and it goes there without a fuss. Chapter eight of the Tao Te Ching looks at that and sees the highest good.
screen: `A GLASS TIPS OVER.` → `IT WENT AROUND.` → `IT FINDS THE LOWEST PLACE.`

segments.voice: First, it benefits all things. The chapter opens by saying the highest good is like water. In Legge's translation: "The excellence of water appears in its benefiting all things." It waters the rose and the weed. It doesn't sort them first. Second, it takes the place nobody wants. Water, the chapter says, settles without striving in the low places that people dislike. And that, it says, is why water is close to the Tao. Everything this week has been pointing here: the valley, the one who goes last, the empty bowl. Water is all of them at once. Third, good ground, deep heart, right timing. Then the chapter does something easy to skip past. It gives a short list of what goodness looks like when it's like water. In a home, it's the ground it stands on. In the heart, depth. In giving, kindness. In speech, being trustworthy. In leading, good order. In work, ability. In action, good timing. Not grand virtues. Ordinary ones, the kind that show up in a kitchen or an office on a weekday. Water isn't only humble. It's also useful, steady and on time. Fourth, it doesn't quarrel. The chapter ends on its plainest line: because water doesn't contend, no one finds fault with it. It doesn't fight the plate. It goes around, and it gets where it was going anyway.
screen: `IT BENEFITS ALL THINGS.` · `IT TAKES THE PLACE NOBODY WANTS.` · `GOOD GROUND, DEEP HEART, RIGHT TIMING.` · `IT DOESN'T QUARREL.` · then, large: `LIKE WATER.`

segments.voice: Today's practice is to pour and watch water. If you can, take a glass of water and pour a little, slowly, into a sink or a bowl or onto a plant. Watch where it goes. See how it doesn't push. It spreads, finds the low point, settles. Then set the glass down and sit with your eyes on the water, or on the memory of it. Breathe slowly, letting each breath settle low in your body, the way the water settled. If you pray, you can pray with the water in front of you. If you don't, just keep watching. The bell holds the time.
Like water. Chapter eight's picture of the highest good: it benefits all things, takes the low place nobody wants, and doesn't quarrel. Today's word.
Your line: like water. The next time something blocks your way today, a person, a rule, a plan, don't push against it. Go around, and keep going. Day one thousand seventy.

howItsDone: Some readers of the Tao Te Ching keep chapter eight's opening words, the highest good is like water, written where they will see them.

original.note: Chinese, shàng shàn ruò shuǐ: the highest good is like water. The opening of Tao Te Ching 8.

trapdoor: what you thought: like water means be soft and go with the flow.
what it means: water benefits all things, takes the low place nobody wants, and doesn't quarrel, and that is why it is near to the Tao.
what a scholar hears: the chapter also lists ordinary goods, ground, depth, kindness, trust, order, ability, timing, and ends on not contending.

sources.quoted: The excellence of water appears in its benefiting all things

sources.ref: Tao Te Ching, chapter 8 (the low places; the list of goods; not contending)

notes: The chapter's list of goods is paraphrased from the Chinese (居善地, 心善淵, 與善仁, 言善信, 正善治, 事善能, 動善時); Legge renders the giving clause as 'associations ... with the virtuous', so 'in giving, kindness' follows other readings. Confirm.
Chapter 8 water was used on days 56 and 1039 (lowness, benefit); this day leans on the list of ordinary goods and the closing line on not contending.
